title: After the Books
subtitle: Stories outlive their physical containers
sourceCredit: Wang Ping · The Moth Radio Hour, “Saving Graces”

shot.title: Under the cloth
shot.direction: The child’s secret books are sheltered by a handmade cloth.
shot.soundDirection: Paper crackle turning gradually into children’s listening breaths and a storyteller’s voice.

illustration.direction: Wide modest courtyard. A girl kneels beside a low wooden chest and carefully tucks a handmade cloth over a small stack of worn books, both hands touching real cloth and paper. She looks toward an unseen doorway with concern. Keep the danger outside the frame and the setting quiet.

shot.title: One bright letter
shot.direction: A single printed letter begins moving before the destructive change.
shot.soundDirection: Paper crackle turning gradually into children’s listening breaths and a storyteller’s voice.

shot.title: They are taking the books
shot.direction: Her hands protect the stack. Keep the threat on the objects, without inventing visible violence against a person.
shot.soundDirection: Paper crackle turning gradually into children’s listening breaths and a storyteller’s voice.

illustration.direction: Same courtyard. The girl draws the books toward her chest with both arms while the cloth falls across her knees. Her expression is alarmed but contained; no visible attacker, uniform, weapon or violence against a body. A loose blank page has lifted slightly in a breeze.

shot.title: Paper catches
shot.direction: A restrained flame overtakes the pages; no body is harmed on screen.
shot.soundDirection: Paper crackle turning gradually into children’s listening breaths and a storyteller’s voice.

illustration.direction: A few books burn in a small restrained outdoor fire on bare stone, separated safely from people. The girl is seen at a distance with empty open hands and lowered shoulders. No body is harmed. Warm firelight is sparse; loss is not immediately covered by magical images.

shot.title: The pages are gone
shot.direction: The destruction has weight. Do not immediately cover it with inspirational imagery.
shot.soundDirection: Paper crackle turning gradually into children’s listening breaths and a storyteller’s voice.

illustration.direction: A few books burn in a small restrained outdoor fire on bare stone, separated safely from people. The girl is seen at a distance with empty open hands and lowered shoulders. No body is harmed. Warm firelight is sparse; loss is not immediately covered by magical images.

shot.title: The ash settles
shot.direction: Empty hands and settling ash establish the loss.
shot.soundDirection: Paper crackle turning gradually into children’s listening breaths and a storyteller’s voice.

illustration.direction: After the fire, the girl sits beside cold grey ash, empty hands resting on her knees. She lifts her face as a small pale abstract paper-like curve appears above her palm, suggesting a first remembered story without readable letters or restored books. The loss stays physically present.

beats.caption: I still remember the first story.

shot.title: A first remembered story
shot.direction: A remembered letter rises above the ash as she starts the story.

shot.title: Someone comes closer
shot.direction: Another child settles within listening distance.
shot.soundDirection: Paper crackle turning gradually into children’s listening breaths and a storyteller’s voice.

illustration.direction: The smaller boy settles on the courtyard step a believable arm’s length from her. He leans forward with an attentive face; she turns toward him and begins a small open-hand storytelling gesture. Both are grounded on the stone step; no book lies between them.

shot.title: What happened next
shot.direction: The listener leans forward; the question gives the storyteller a next action.

shot.title: Memory becomes invention
shot.direction: Preserve both remembered and invented parts of her telling. Small imagined shapes take the place of the missing pages.
shot.soundDirection: Paper crackle turning gradually into children’s listening breaths and a storyteller’s voice.

illustration.direction: A small attentive circle of distinct children sits around the girl on the same step. She tells a story with one modest hand gesture; tiny faint imagined shapes appear only behind her, not as a replacement pile of books. Empty cloth and distant ash remain. Human listening carries the ending.

shot.title: An attentive circle
shot.direction: Attention passes between faces, not through a restored physical book.
